sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere (grep stress/accent = 0). Sect. 8.3 'Phonetic inventory' covers only Cha'ari, Dokshi, Dyarim and Tulai wordlists; sect. 4.5 (printed p.4, PDF p.12): 'The wordlists were collected in Cha'ari, Dokshi, Dyarim, and Tulai. The Zeem people were unable to provide words in their heritage language.'; sect. 5.1.5 (printed p.7, PDF p.15): 'Since Zeem is no longer spoken (see § 8)'; sect. 3 (printed p.2): 'In 1978, Shimizu published a small amount of data on Zeem, Cha'ari, and Dokshi.'; App. F: 'no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features'…

PDF p.8: 'Cààrí is the only surviving language of the Zeem subgroup, the other three (Zeem, Tule and Dokshi) being extinct'; p.3 'Zaar and Gùùs have three tone levels, the others only two' refers to the five sampled lects (Chaari standing in for the Zeem cluster), not to Zeem proper, which Caron never recorded; p.20 lists Zeem among lects that are 'dying' with 'a handful' of speakers.
